headline: Cave Tours and Monument Access Reservations
reservation: Cave tours at Wind Cave and Jewel Cave often sell out weeks in advance; booking via the official NPS portal is essential. Mount Rushmore does not require entry reservations but charges a parking fee. Check for seasonal changes in tour availability and monument hours on official government websites.

days.title: Monuments and Spires

stops.name: Mount Rushmore National Memorial
stops.detail: View the iconic carvings and explore the Presidential Trail to see the mountain from different angles.

stops.name: Needles Highway
stops.detail: Drive through unique granite 'needles' and narrow tunnels that define the central Black Hills landscape.

days.driving: Allow 2 to 3 hours for winding scenic roads; conditions vary.
days.note: Check vehicle clearance for the Needles Eye Tunnel; RVs may be restricted.

days.title: Wildlife and High Peaks

stops.name: Black Elk Peak
stops.detail: Hike from Sylvan Lake to the highest point in South Dakota for a panoramic view of the hills.

stops.name: Wildlife Loop Road
stops.detail: Observe free-roaming bison, burros, and pronghorn in the grasslands of Custer State Park.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for wildlife viewing and transit; conditions vary.
days.note: Maintain a safe distance from bison; they are wild and unpredictable.

days.title: Subterranean and Northern Hills

stops.name: Wind Cave National Park
stops.detail: Take a guided tour to see rare boxwork formations in one of the world's longest caves.

stops.name: Spearfish Canyon
stops.detail: Drive the scenic byway in the north to see limestone cliffs and waterfalls like Bridal Veil.

days.driving: Allow 3 to 4 hours for the full north-south transit; conditions vary.
days.note: Cave temperatures are a constant 54 degrees; bring a jacket regardless of surface weather.

intel.title: Sylvan Lake Congestion
intel.text: Parking at Sylvan Lake and Mount Rushmore is high-demand and can reach capacity by midday. Arrive early or use overflow lots where permitted.

intel.title: Forested Dead Zones
intel.text: Cell service is spotty throughout the Black Hills National Forest and within Custer State Park. Carry physical maps for navigating winding interior roads.

intel.title: Town-Based Services
intel.text: Gas stations are concentrated in Custer, Hill City, and Rapid City. Ensure a full tank before starting the Wildlife Loop or Spearfish Canyon drives.

intel.title: Sturgis Rally Impact
intel.text: Early August brings significant traffic and limited lodging due to the motorcycle rally. Plan for much slower travel times and book a year in advance for this window.

intel.title: Tunnel Clearance
intel.text: Iron Mountain Road and Needles Highway feature extremely narrow tunnels. Verify your vehicle dimensions against posted limits before attempting these routes.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Rapid City Regional Airport (RAP), pick up your vehicle, and drive 45–60 minutes to Custer or Hill City for lodging.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are ideal for winding roads; large RVs face significant restrictions on scenic highways.
plan.goldenHour: Norbeck Overlook for views of the granite spires and Mount Rushmore during the late afternoon glow.
